scope: Methods research before new motorcycle modeling
selected_method: Multi-view dimension-constrained modeling by component with explicit camera verification

sources.title: fSpy — Basics
sources.application_note: Perspective calibration assumptions and limits; use only where justified vanishing directions exist.

sources.title: fSpy — Tutorial
sources.application_note: Reference distance anchors scale after a suitable calibration; guides help inspect the solution.

sources.title: COLMAP — Tutorial
sources.application_note: Textured overlap and stable image evidence matter; automatic reconstruction is not guaranteed for this dataset.

sources.title: Agisoft — Close-range objects scanning
sources.application_note: Reflective/transparent surfaces and turntable backgrounds complicate capture and reconstruction.

sources.title: Eldar Seydamet — Making a Honda Bike with Maya & UE4
sources.application_note: Useful real-bike production workflow; no asset, paid software, exact budget or timeline copied.

sources.title: Alexa Ranzola — How to Model a Realistic Bike Based on a2013 Harley Davidson Sportster
sources.application_note: Separate components and a clean control material version before wear; example scope differs from browser game.

sources.title: Lautaro Iglesias — Futuristic Racing Motorcycle
sources.application_note: Single-view composition shortcuts explicitly unsuitable as a complete moving motorcycle.

sources.title: Blender Artists — Aligning object perspective
sources.application_note: Practical example of focal-length mismatch; not a calibration result for our images.

sources.title: Khronos — Physically Based Rendering in glTF
sources.application_note: Material channels and extensions for engine export and inspection.

sources.title: Khronos — glTF2.0 Specification
sources.application_note: Units and texture data conventions; technical format compliance does not certify realism.

sources.title: CG Cookie — Modeling a Motorcycle
sources.application_note: Public outline read; no paid lesson watched or bought; its free interpretation of reference not adopted.
